description: We are a team of motivated students from Almaty, Kazakhstan, passionate about science, technology, programming, and space exploration. We enjoy creative problem-solving and building innovative projects. We are looking for teammates skilled in programming, web development, Python, UI/UX design, 3D modeling, GIS, and Earth science. Curiosity, creativity, and teamwork are always welcome. Let's build something amazing together! 🚀
summary:
**EarthPulse** is an interactive, browser-based emergency monitoring platform that bridges a critical gap in disaster response: making advanced synthetic aperture radar (SAR) analysis accessible to everyone in real time.

Addressing the reality that millions of people are affected by disasters annually—often under heavy cloud cover where optical satellites are blind—EarthPulse aggregates live hazard data from USGS, NASA, and GDACS onto an interactive 3D globe. With a single tap on any event, users can launch the Radar Lab to compare pre- and post-disaster NASA OPERA radar passes. By leveraging microwave pulses that penetrate clouds, day or night, EarthPulse automatically calculates flooded surface areas and terrain changes in square kilometers.

This project is vital because over 40% of countries lack multi-hazard early warning systems, and traditional damage assessment takes days. EarthPulse empowers first responders, local authorities, journalists, and affected communities with rapid, cloud-penetrating scientific evidence—delivering actionable situational awareness directly to any mobile browser without requiring installations or specialized software.
details:
EarthPulse is a radar emergency monitor that runs in any phone browser with no account or install. It shows live earthquakes, wildfires, storms, volcanoes and floods (USGS, NASA EONET, GDACS) on one 3D globe. When a user taps an event, the app finds the Sentinel-1 radar passes before and after it (NASA CMR). It loads NASA OPERA products through GIBS and shows a before/after comparison with the change measured in km². Radar sees through cloud, smoke and darkness, so floods can be measured when optical cameras see only cloud.

The goal is to give responders, local authorities, journalists and ordinary people a fast first estimate of the damage where early warning systems are missing. Radar analysis normally needs specialist software, and here it takes one tap. Each result is stated as a hypothesis with a way to test it, and the app lists its limits. The project is a single HTML file built with JavaScript, WebGL2 shaders, D3.js and NASA APIs, with no backend.
dataRefs: NASA OPERA DSWx-S1 (Dynamic Surface Water Extent from Sentinel-1)
NASA OPERA RTC-S1 (Radiometric Terrain Corrected SAR Backscatter)
